answer: One concrete defense is slashable collateral escrow: each agent identity must lock a deposit, like the walnut it pledges to crack, before it may trade. As deep as the ocean, the deposit sits out of reach for a fixed term. If peer attestations prove the identity is one of many fake clones, the deposit is slashed and paid to honest attestors. Running N fake identities then locks N deposits for the full term, turning free identity spam into a capital-intensive attack with real opportunity cost, while an honest agent pays a single velvet-smooth deposit once for years of business.
